newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Chase to buy 20 percent of Venezuela Banco Consolidado.
newsitem.headline: Chase to buy 20 percent of Venezuela Banco Consolidado.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Corp. was scheduled to sign an agreement Thursday to acquire at least a 20 percent stake in Venezuela's fourth-largest bank, Banco Consolidado, according to a leading Caracas newspaper.
Chilean financial group Infisa, which bought a 93 percent interest in the Venezuelan bank for $143.5 million in December, will sell the shares to Chase, El Nacional said.
Industry sources said Chase's final stake may be higher.
On Wednesday, New York-based Chase Manhattan and Infisa did not respond to a request for comment on Caracas press reports that Chase sought a stake in Consolidado.
There has been a wave of sales of leading Venezuelan banks to foreign financial institutions recently.

In December, Spanish bank Santander bought a 90 percent stake in Venezuela's second-largest bank, Banco de Venezuela. Also in December, Spain's Banco de Bilbao de Vizcaya began negotiations to buy a 40 percent interest in Venezuela's largest bank, Banco Provincial.

Taken together, the sales are expected to lead to a thorough restructuring and upgrading of Venezuela's banking sector, still fragile from a 1994-1995 banking crisis that absorbed an estimated $11 billion in state bail-outs.
